title: VPC Probe Orchestrator: API priming, staged model loading, and SLO validation
creator: Mei Chen
description: Create an automated "VPC Probe Orchestrator" that runs immediately after Terraform applies for Private (VPC) deployments. The orchestrator will perform sequenced post-deploy checks: API readiness, authentication & network validation, staged model priming (KV/prefix warmup + small-request priming), constrained concurrency load tests, and a short smoke verification of common routes (generation, chat, embeddings). The goal is to provide a deterministic acceptance signal (PASS/FAIL + diagnostics) that gates rollout and surfaces actionable telemetry to the Console dashboards and on-call SREs.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Terraform post-apply triggers orchestrator and returns a pass/fail state within 10 minutes
A2: /health and /ready endpoints report OK and auth checks succeed for service account
A3: Representative model artifacts successfully loaded and visible in runtime logs (model_load_time < 60s)
A4: KV cache priming completes and reduces token latency by >=10% on a representative prompt set
A5: Concurrency ramp test shows error rate < 0.5% at target commit throughput (configurable per customer)
A6: On failure, orchestrator records diagnostics (logs, metrics snapshot, last 100 responses) and creates/updates the Linear ticket with a link to failure artifacts
runbook_steps: Step 0: Trigger - Terraform null_resource post-apply executes orchestrator Lambda/Job with deployment metadata and credentials
Step 1: Wait for K8s / ECS service readiness - poll service API until 2x successful /ready responses within 30s windows
Step 2: Auth smoke - perform token exchange for service principal and call /whoami to validate IAM / VPC path
Step 3: API surface smoke - hit /generate, /chat, /embed with minimal payloads and validate HTTP 200 + schema match

Step 4: Model priming - for each model variant configured for this deployment: send 8 short representative prompts to populate KV/prefix cache and to load attention caches (order: small -> medium -> large)
Step 5: Warm KV validation - measure avg token latency before/after priming using a fixed prompt set and assert improvement threshold
Step 6: Staged concurrency ramp - run 1m windows at concurrency=[1,5,20,50] or until configured commit; record p50/p95/p99, error rate, token throughput
Step 7: Resource sanity checks - verify GPU memory < 90%, process RSS stable, model loader thread counts within expected bounds
Step 8: Model load time check - ensure first token arrival for each model variant < 60s post-priming; collect runtime stacktrace if > 60s
Step 9: SLO evaluation - compare measured latency/error figures against tenant SLOs and acceptance criteria
Step 10: Report - upload artifacts to deployment bucket, post summary to Console ticketing channel, and mark orchestrator outcome in Terraform state as 'ready' or 'needs-attention'
metrics_and_thresholds: error_rate < 0.5% across smoke and ramp windows
disk_io and network egress within expected deployment baselines
automation_hooks: Terraform: null_resource with local-exec calling orchestration API (https://orchestrator.internal/deployments/:id/trigger)
K8s Job: fallback runner for private air-gapped installs that calls the same orchestrator logic
GitHub Actions: optional PR gate that can simulate the orchestrator with a fake VPC to catch regressions in CI
Console: webhook to post summary and include links to detailed logs/dashboards
Retries: exponential backoff configuration (2 retries, 30s -> 120s) for flakey network validation steps
test_matrix: Model sizes: tiny (ggml-style), base, large; verify each loads and responds
Sequence lengths: short(32), medium(256), long(1024) - validate latency and memory behavior
Concurrency steps: 1, 5, 20, 50 (or scaled to tenant commit) with 60s windows
Prompt types: generate (100B tokens), chat (system + 2 messages), embed (short vector payload)
Network topologies: same-subnet, cross-subnet, cross-AZ - ensure endpoints reachable via configured routing rules
